How a cause is decided

A move counts as abnormal against Bitcoin's own recent scale, so a quiet week and a wild week are judged by different rulers. For each one we check what was measurable at that minute: news that landed before or as it started, liquidations from our own collector, trades by tracked Hyperliquid whales, and open interest rising or falling with the price.

Only the first report counts

A story that breaks and is then repeated by forty outlets is one piece of news. A move can be credited only to the first report of a story, so a recap written after the drop cannot claim to have caused it. The repeats only raise how much that story mattered. Every event is on the live catalyst list.

Why some moves have no answer

If nothing measurable explains a move, the row says so rather than borrowing the nearest headline. Most real moves also have more than one cause, so a large drop can be a piece of news that started it and a liquidation cascade that finished it. A forced close is a market order, which is how a small drop turns into a long one.

Questions

Why is Bitcoin down today?

The box at the top of this page answers it with the current figure: the 24-hour change, the biggest move inside it, and what we measured at that minute. If nothing measurable explains it, it says that instead of guessing.

Why does Bitcoin crash so fast?

Because a falling price forces leveraged longs out. A liquidation is a market sell, so it pushes the price into the next group of liquidations. That chain is a cascade, and it is why a drop can run far past whatever started it.

Is the news always the reason?

No. Over a month many Bitcoin moves come from positioning alone: liquidations, whales or open interest with no news at all. A headline written after a drop is usually a description of it rather than its cause.

Does this work when Bitcoin is going up?

Yes. The page reads every abnormal move in either direction, and a jump is judged by the same rules, including short squeezes.

What about other coins?

The same reading exists for every market MarginPad charts. Turn on What moved it on a chart, or ask the free JSON with another symbol.
